ticket.title: chalkline-core: declare a task-writing port so the edge to storypole-core burns
acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-06, commit f32d87b (chalkline). First of the three behavioral GB-204 edges burned.

chalkline-core no longer depends on storypole-core at all: the dependency is gone from its manifest, not merely unused. DagCompiler::compile now takes &mut impl TaskSink and emits CompiledTask values; the port has exactly two methods (create, link_blocked_by) because every method on it is one the sink author keeps working forever. StorypoleSink implements it in chalkline-mcp, which is an integrator and may hold the edge, and chalkline-cli reuses it because it already depends on chalkline-mcp - so there is no duplication and no integrator-to-integrator edge either.

Layers: lateral allowlist 4 -> 3, downward 147 -> 148, verdict clean. The stale allowlist entry this left behind had to be deleted by hand, which is exactly the hole GB-248 describes (the gate does not fail on an entry matching no edge).

Bonus fix, same failure class as GB-282: chalkline's resolve_spec_file and grill handler probed SPEC.md at the repository root only, so after the docs move every specification read as missing with no error. Both probe docs/ then the root now.

Test improvement worth noting: the old test needed a real storypole store to assert anything. The recording sink asserts the emitted tasks and the exact (child, blocker) pair, which is a strictly stronger claim and needs no engine.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, 29 tests green, docs check 9 present 0 drifted.

Separate finding filed: cargo nextest run at the chalkline root discovers 0 tests and exits 4 - the workspace's test targets are only found when packages are named explicitly.
